UK-BVI Arrangement for the Exchange of Information on Tax Matters

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/692, as amended); Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (UK); Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018 (UK); BVI Business Companies Act 2004 (as amended), Part XI (Beneficial Ownership Register); BVI Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) Regulations 2017; BVI Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Code of Practice 2023; BVI Economic Substance (Companies and Limited Partnerships) Act 2018.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (each UBO and signatory)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority with notarization by a licensed notary in the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or duly licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional reference letter from an existing regulated institution
Certificate of Incumbency or corporate extract for any intermediary corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BVI registered agent or competent foreign company registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private internal document; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UK HM Treasury Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated list, US OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated list, BVI Financial Services Commission sanctions list, and Interpol notices. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, family members, close associates, and any red-flag triggers under the BVI Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Code of Practice. Verification must be refreshed every 90 days during the pre-incorporation process and thereafter on a risk-sensitive basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BVI Financial Services Commission (FSC) – Registry of Corporate Affairs online name reservation and filing portal, accessible through FSC-licensed registered agents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: BVI law requires corporate names in Latin characters; English-language suffixes are mandatory. Names may include numerals and permitted special characters only as specified in the BVI Business Companies Act. Where a foreign-language name is used, a statutory transliteration into Latin script is required and subject to registry acceptance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant, through its BVI registered agent, must file a written request for reconsideration with the BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs within 14 days of the rejection notice. The request must include a detailed explanation and, where relevant, evidence of prior ministerial or regulator consent for a sensitive token. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may pursue judicial review before the BVI Commercial Court of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court. Alternatively, a fresh name application with a corrected sensitive-token consent may be filed without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for BVI BC formation; a physical registered office in the BVI and a licensed BVI registered agent are mandatory. A virtual office cannot substitute for statutory registered-office requirements, although certain administrative functions such as bookkeeping and board-meeting coordination may be performed remotely.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk, estimated at under 5% annually for a non-regulated Micro-SaaS company; however, the likelihood rises if economic substance obligations apply or if the company engages in any BVI 'relevant activity' under the Economic Substance Act. The BVI FSC may carry out unannounced on-site inspections on a risk-proportionate basis.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 (as amended), Part II (Incorporation, sections 7-16); Part VI (Directors and Officers); implemented under the BVI Companies Regulations, 2019.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission, Road Town, Tortola, British Virgin Islands (electronic filing via the VIRRGIN online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital applies. A BVI Business Company may be incorporated with nil or a single no-par-value share; capital may be designated in any currency and no escrow or capital deposit requirement exists at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company be and they are hereby adopted in the form filed with the Registrar. RESOLVED, that the allotment of subscriber shares to the initial member be ratified and share certificates issued. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established at the address of the registered agent. RESOLVED, that [Director Name] be appointed as first Director and [Officer Name] as Secretary, each to act until removed by resolution. RESOLVED, that the Director is authorized to open corporate bank and merchant accounts, including EMI and payment-processor mandates with Paddle and Lemon Squeezy, and to execute all account documentation. RESOLVED, that all acts of the subscribers in furthering incorporation be ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of BVI-Licensed Registered Agent and Company Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI-licensed registered agent (regulated by the BVI Financial Services Commission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select and engage a BVI-licensed registered agent. Complete client onboarding and KYC/AML verification. Instruct the agent to run a name search in the VIRRGIN registry system and reserve the proposed company name. Execute the registered agent engagement letter and corporate services agreement, and supply identification documents for the subscriber and intended directors.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter and corporate services agreement
Company name reservation request (agent-prepared) with two alternative names
Certified copy of the passport of each subscriber and director
Proof of residential address dated within the last 3 months
Commercial bank reference or professional reference for each director
Beneficial ownership register questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or conflicts with an existing registered name, the agent re-submits an alternative from the reserved name list at no additional government fee; the refreshed search is processed within 1 business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Electronic Filing of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission (VIRRGIN portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the M&AA reflecting authorized share capital up to USD 50,000 (standard government fee band), no-minimum-capital election, and broad object powers. The subscriber executes the M&AA and the incorporation application, including the notice of registered agent and registered office address, and submits the full package electronically through VIRRGIN.
required_dossiers: Drafted and executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Subscriber consent to incorporation
Consent of first director to act
Notice of registered agent and registered office address
Government fee payment authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises a query on the M&AA or consents, the agent amends the documents and re-files through VIRRGIN; a first query is cured without penalty, typically within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Settlement of Government Fees and Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance of the incorporation application, the Registry collects the USD 350 government fee and issues a digitally signed Certificate of Incorporation together with an extract of the BVI Business Company register. The registered agent downloads the certificate and establishes the statutory registers (members, directors, and charges), and prepares physical or electronic share certificates.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Extract of the BVI Business Company register
Fully registered Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent certificate
Statutory register templates and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains typographical errors, a correction request is filed with the Registry; processing takes approximately 2 business days and no material correction fee is assessed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural Board Meeting and Adoption of Corporate Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company (or written resolution procedure under the BVI Business Companies Act, 2004)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering adoption of the M&AA, ratification of subscriber share allotment, establishment of the registered office address, appointment of the first director and officers, and authorization to open corporate bank and EMI accounts and to execute payment-processor mandates with Paddle and Lemon Squeezy. File executed minutes and resolutions in the Company minute book maintained at the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the inaugural board meeting
Written resolutions in lieu of meeting (if applicable)
Consent to act of each director and secretary
Share certificate issued to the founding member
Copy of the adopted pro-forma first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment or allotment is defective, the Board passes a subsequent ratifying resolution; internal governance defects do not require re-filing with the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: United Kingdom Ancillary Registrations and Commencement of Trading Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House (United Kingdom) and Information Commissioner's Office (United Kingdom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the BVI Company establishes a UK establishment (physical office or employees present in the UK), file Form OS1 with Companies House within one month of establishment; if no UK establishment exists, no Companies House filing is required. Where the Company processes personal data of UK consumers through its SaaS platform, file a data-protection notification with the ICO and pay the annual data-protection fee. Issue a Certificate of Good Standing from the BVI Registry as part of final onboarding documentation for banking and payment partners.
required_dossiers: Form OS1 (registration of a UK establishment, if applicable)
Certified English translation of the Certificate of Incorporation and M&AA
Form OS2 (list of directors and secretary)
Form OS4 (persons with significant control)
ICO data-protection notification and fee payment
BVI Certificate of Good Standing (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Companies House rejects incomplete OS1 filings; remedy by correcting and re-filing within 14 days, though late filing attracts a civil penalty, so a UK filing agent is engaged to expedite. ICO notification errors may be rectified online through the ICO portal without penalty if corrected within 28 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 cloud software operations require no manufacturing or industrial operating license in the United Kingdom. For data-processing compliance the relevant authority is the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), United Kingdom.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None - no statutory operating or manufacturing permit applies to the provision of consumer micro-SaaS subscription services in the United Kingdom.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable - no environmental regulator is engaged for purely digital operations (reference regulator in the UK: Environment Agency).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Environmental Impact Assessment is required. The activity does not fall within Schedule 1 or Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 2017 because no physical development, land-use change, or industrial installation occurs.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process discharges or emissions are generated by cloud software activity. If IT hardware is introduced, compliance applies under the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) Regulations 2013 and the Environmental Protection Act 1990 duty of care; e-waste must be transferred only to licensed waste carriers, and data-center hosting is to be arranged exclusively with WEEE-registered providers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-safety certificate or structural load inspection is required for virtual-office or home-office software operations. If a serviced office or data-center co-location is used, the landlord or operator holds the fire risk assessment under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 and the relevant building-control approvals. For any UK-based staff, the employer must comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Display Screen Equipment Regulations 1992 (workstation self-assessments), and the Employers' Liability (Compulsory Insurance) Act 1969.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC); official online portal: https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/hm-revenue-customs
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The target entity is a BVI Business Company (BC) which, under BVI law, is tax-exempt. For UK tax purposes the BC is treated as a foreign company, not as a pass-through entity. The BC must register for UK VAT as a non-established taxable person if it makes any taxable supplies in the UK from which UK VAT is chargeable. For SaaS/digital services supplied to UK private consumers, the place of supply is the UK and the non-established supplier has a mandatory VAT registration obligation from the first supply, with no UK turnover threshold. Registration procedure: complete HMRC form VAT1 (for non-EU/non-UK established businesses) or use the HMRC online VAT registration service for non-established taxable persons; provide the BVI Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, evidence of business activity (website/subscription platform, merchant agreements with Paddle or Lemon Squeezy, sample invoices), bank account reference from an eligible EMI or bank, and, if appointed, details of a UK tax representative. HMRC will issue a 9-digit GB VAT registration number. For UK Corporation Tax, a non-UK resident company is registrable only if it carries on a trade in the UK through a permanent establishment. If a UK PE exists, the BC must register for Corporation Tax within 3 months of commencing UK activity using form CT41G and HMRC will issue a 10-digit Unique Taxpayer Reference. If no UK PE exists, no UK Corporation Tax registration is required. Where Paddle or Lemon Squeezy acts as Merchant of Record, the platform may be the supplier of the underlying services to the end consumer and may account for UK VAT; in that case, separate UK VAT registration by the BC may not be required, but contractual allocation of VAT liability must be documented and confirmed by legal advice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The UK does not operate a check-the-box regime for foreign entities. The BVI BC is an opaque, separately taxable entity for UK tax; it cannot elect transparent/pass-through treatment. There is no hybrid mismatch election available; the UK hybrid mismatch rules in CTA 2010 Part 6A operate automatically to recharacterise payments where there is a mismatch in tax treatment. For VAT, a non-established taxable person may elect to register voluntarily before making supplies and may, if it has a UK fixed establishment, apply to join a UK VAT group. If the BC has a UK permanent establishment, it may make a UK PE notification and is required to apply arm's length attribution to the PE under the UK transfer pricing rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act 1994
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for non-established taxable persons; the annual registration threshold of GBP 85,000 applies only to UK-established businesses. A BVI BC supplying digital services to UK consumers must register from the first supply because the place of supply is the UK.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The UK does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control mandate. E-invoices are permitted and must satisfy VAT invoicing content requirements. VAT returns must be filed electronically via HMRC's Making Tax Digital (MTD) system for VAT using MTD-compatible software; businesses must keep digital records and submit returns using functional compatible software. No prior HMRC fiscal authorisation is required for the issuance of individual invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For the target Micro-SaaS business, the principal supplies are digital services, not physical goods. Zero-rating for goods applies only where physical goods are exported from the UK to a destination outside the UK within the time limits in the Export (Goods) Order 2000: the goods must be removed to a non-UK destination within 3 months of supply; the supplier must hold evidence of export in the form of official customs documents and transport documents; the recipient must be outside the UK; and the export must satisfy HMRC's direct or indirect export conditions. Digital services supplied B2C to UK consumers are subject to UK VAT at 20% and are not zero-rated; digital services supplied to non-UK business customers or non-UK consumers fall outside the scope of UK VAT because the place of supply is outside the UK, rather than being zero-rated exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/C88 submitted via the UK Customs Declaration Service or National Export System)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR consignment note or recognised courier shipment evidence
Commercial invoice and export sales contract
Bank transfer / SWIFT / remittance certificate evidencing receipt of foreign currency consideration
Evidence of non-UK customer status (overseas VAT registration number or tax identification number)
Export packing list and freight invoices substantiating physical removal from the UK
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may deny or claw back zero-rating where export evidence is incomplete, inconsistent, or obtained after the supply. Where zero-rating is denied, HMRC may issue an assessment for the unpaid UK VAT, plus statutory interest from the date the VAT should have been accounted. Civil penalties for inaccuracy or tax evasion may be imposed under Schedule 24 Finance Act 2007: careless inaccuracy attracts up to 30% of the potential lost revenue; deliberate but unconcealed acts up to 70%; deliberate and concealed acts up to 100%, reduced for prompt or unprompted disclosure. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion of VAT may be pursued under Section 72 Value Added Tax Act 1994, carrying unlimited fines and imprisonment. Assessment and clawback time limits are generally 4 years, extended to 20 years where fraud or deliberate non-disclosure is involved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Governor and Company of the Bank of England (the Bank of England) acting jointly with HM Treasury for exchange-control policy; the Prudential Regulation Authority (UK) as the micro-prudential banking supervisor; His Majesty's Revenue and Customs as the anti-money-laundering and transaction-reporting authority under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United Kingdom operates a fully liberalised foreign-exchange regime. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible; no prior authorisation is required for purchases or sales of foreign currency. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, and liquidation proceeds may be remitted abroad without restriction, subject only to standard AML/CFT verification and, where relevant, taxation under UK source rules or double-taxation relief. The BVI Business Company is a non-resident entity for UK tax purposes unless UK management and control are exercised; a zero-rate BVI tax profile does not create a UK remittance restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no UK statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirements for export receipts. The Exchange Control Act 1947 was repealed in 1979; exporters and service providers may retain, convert, or repatriate foreign currency freely. For statistical and financial-prudential reporting, UK banks apply Balance of Payments reporting codes for cross-border credits and may require supporting trade documents, but no percentage of export proceeds must be surrendered to the Bank of England or converted into sterling.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for an FCA-authorised or EEA-passported Electronic Money Institution such as Revolut Business, Tide, or Wise Business. Such EMIs routinely accept BVI corporate clients when final beneficial owners are disclosed and supporting substance documents are provided. Legal constraints are material: the EMI must hold safeguarding accounts for client funds, use EEA or UK payment clearing rails, and must not be used as a substitute for a full-service corporate bank. Unregulated offshore digital EMIs are not viable and should be rejected for treasury purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The UK Money Laundering Regulations 2017 permit remote customer due diligence and video-verified KYC interviews. In practice, tier-1 UK banks require an in-person or video interview with the natural-person directors of a non-resident BVI Business Company before account activation. Physical attendance in the UK is not statutorily mandatory, but many relationship managers demand a London meeting or a recognised introducer meeting; remote-only onboarding is available only through fintech EMIs and selected challenger banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BVI offshore jurisdiction classification and macro-prudential de-risking by UK banks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certificate of good standing from the BVI Financial Services Commission, certified certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, registered agent confirmation letter, BVI registered office certificate, BVI REGS beneficial-ownership screening evidence, and a board resolution naming the UK bank account and signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No UK physical or tax nexus for a non-resident BVI company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a UK registered-office or virtual-office service agreement, director and shareholder residential addresses, management-accounts letter explaining operational substance in the BVI or other jurisdictions, confirmation of non-UK tax residence, and a written explanation of the commercial purpose for maintaining sterling liquidity in the UK.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholding or opaque UBO structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply executed nominee declaration and trust deed, identity and proof of address for every beneficial owner holding more than 25% of the BVI company, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation for each owner, and an independent legal opinion confirming the beneficial-ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid digital revenue inflows from consumer micro-SaaS subscriptions triggering perceived money-laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide at least six months of payment-provider payout statements from Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, Stripe, or FastSpring, the Micro-SaaS revenue dashboard, sample subscription agreements, terms of service, privacy policy, tax registration evidence, and a letter from a licensed accountant confirming revenue traceability and platform settlement logic.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound capital contributions through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the BVI shareholder's bank to the UK corporate account. Use the payment narrative 'DIRECT INVESTMENT – SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' and the bank's accepted Balance of Payments purpose code for direct investment inwards (typically D.3 or the bank-specific code for equity capital; confirm the exact code with the receiving UK treasury desk). Attach the board resolution authorising the allotment, updated register of members, share certificate, and a source-of-funds declaration. Sterling-denominated transfers may be settled via CHAPS for immediate finality.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for low-value and medium-value supplier and vendor payments, with full beneficiary bank details and purpose narrative. For larger disbursements, SWIFT MT202/MT202COV may be used after the corresponding MT103; for physical-goods trade, issue a commercial letter of credit through the UK issuing bank using SWIFT MT700 and MT707 amendments. Euro-denominated payouts across the single euro payments area should be cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer; urgent sterling disbursements should be routed over CHAPS. All outbound wires must be matched against an approved vendor file and procurement board resolution to maintain audit trail integrity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards between GBP, USD, and EUR to hedge subscription-revenue and supplier-cost timing mismatches
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps) for longer-dated balance-sheet risk or repeated repatriation cycles
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for high-exposure currencies lacking onshore deliverability, executed only with a regulated UK bank or FCA-authorised broker

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Financial Services Commission (via registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late penalty if payment is not made by 31 May; failure for six months or more exposes company to administrative strike-off by the Registrar of Corporate Affairs and restoration costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Economic Substance Annual Return / Non-Application Declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the company's financial year end; for a 31 December year end, filing and payment are due not later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may attract daily penalty and financial penalties imposed by the ITA; continuing default may lead to enforcement action and liability for tax information exchange consequences

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System (BOSS) annual updater
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Financial Services Commission via the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing required within 14 days of each relevant change; annual confirmation to registered agent not later than the company's annual government fee due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default fines up to US$20,000 for the company and responsible officers; removal from register possible for persistent non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: BVI law does not impose a statutory audit threshold or require audited accounts for a micro SaaS BVI business company; accounts may be prepared internally unless a shareholder resolution, lender, or economic substance return requires audited financials
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is the accepted benchmark for BVI companies preparing voluntary financial statements and for Economic Substance Return financial data

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must identify all beneficial owners and file their particulars on the BOSS system; the company must notify the agent of any transfer, new indirect holder, or change in nature of control within 14 days, and a full annual confirmation should be completed before the 31 May government-fee date
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (held by registered agent in BVI)
